messages:
Alex M: quick async roundup from me — pushed the gw routing patch that adds weighted fallback for model variants. hits local tests, need a review on the config merge (PR 4821).
Priya K: taking a look now. main thing i want to check is the priority inversion when both auth and rate checks fail.
Jamal R: blocker: noticed flaky test in staging where the token-bucket counter drifts under burst=400. repro steps in the PR comments.
Serena L: saw that too. probably the atomic increment in the redis LUA needs a TTL refresh. i can experiment.
Dmitri V: heads-up: i'm rolling a tiny auth-change (nhs header passthrough) that could change route keys. holding canary until Alex's config lands.
Alex M: noted. PR includes a mapping transform but not the passthrough change — will coordinate merge order.
Priya K: quick question re rate limits — should we use per-customer or per-route for the new model routing? my vote: per-customer with per-route caps on top.
Jamal R: agree per-customer default, because bursts from many routes can otherwise kill a single tenant.
Serena L: +1. I'll sketch a rollout plan: Phase 1 enable per-customer soft-limits (no hard reject), Phase 2 enforce. Want to avoid surprise 429s.
Alex M: plan sounds good. Serena, can you post the rollout snippet? a small example is enough.
Serena L: sure — example for the cfg: ```json
{
  "policy_id": "route_throttle_v2",
  "scope": "customer",
  "limits": {"window_s": 60, "tokens": 600, "burst": 200},
  "overage_action": "soft_warn"
}
```
Priya K: looks good. From an auth perspective, if overage_action=hard_reject later we'll return 401 or 429? prefer 429 for rate but 401 for auth failures.
Dmitri V: yes keep semantics consistent — gateway should return 401 for auth, 429 for rate. i added tests for that in my branch.
deploy-bot: Canary deployed: gw-service v2.14.0 -> eu-west-1 (canary=10%) — logs: https://deploys.internal/reports/1718899999
Jamal R: i skimmed the canary logs — seeing a small uptick in latency for requests with KV-cache miss + auth header rewrite. could be serialization overhead.
Alex M: ok i'll add a micro-optim to the serializer (avoid copying the headers if passthrough==true).
Priya K: also pinging @Serena L for a code review on the lua rate limiter tweak — i left inline comments.
Serena L: will review after lunch. if everything passes i can start the per-customer soft rollout tomorrow morning.
Alex M: blockers: none from my side after patch, just need approvals.
Jamal R: blockers: need someone to ack the staging test fix before i flip the flag.
Dmitri V: i'll carve out 30m after standup to help reproduce and fix the redis ttl race.
Priya K: i'll review PR 4821 and the routing mapping today. aim to merge by EOD if green.
Alex M: thanks. And FYI — if anyone sees weird 502s during canary reduce canary to 1% and tag me.
Serena L: noted. i'll post a quick playbook in ops channel if we have to roll back.
Alex M: closing — post any follow-ups here. :thumbsup:
